title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated‑repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic netops validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation reused for both conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (validator + ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern is to pair a generative model with a deterministic validator and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. The measurable benefit of this guarded pattern depends on what is held fixed (the estimand), single‑shot generator quality, validator expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates the deterministic rescue obtainable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate (the identical candidate was used in both arms) and compared: (a) baseline — accept the candidate without repair; and (b) guarded — run a deterministic validator and permit at most one automated, constrained repair followed by re‑validation. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle (archived) including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Prior work demonstrates active use of LLMs in NetOps tasks (intent translation, template synthesis, protocol test generation, and repair) and emphasizes tool augmentation to improve correctness [1]–[5]. Planner‑centric frameworks and ReAct‑style tool‑use architectures allow LLMs to call external validators or synthesizers to coordinate multi‑step workflows and reduce end‑to‑end risk [6]. Empirical reports show that introducing deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve correctness relative to unconstrained generation, but the magnitude varies with validator coverage, task distribution, and whether resampling is permitted [3],[4].

Methodological themes motivating our design are: (i) evaluations that conflate benefits from deterministic validation with benefits from resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration make it hard to bound the rescue attributable to post‑generation checking alone; and (ii) many available NetOps benchmarks emphasize syntactic/template correctness rather than semantically rich invariants (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation), limiting operational generality. Our study explicitly conditions on a single LLM draw per intent to quantify the bounded, post‑hoc verifier/repair effect absent resampling, addressing a gap highlighted in these prior surveys and system reports [1]–[4].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and the confirmatory estimand is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents after applying prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The analysis executor and multiplicity plan were fixed prior to the main run.

Task suite and stratification. Tasks were generated deterministically into a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty levels (low/medium/high); the confirmatory sample included 100 pairs per stratum. Each task manifest encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final device states, sequencing invariants (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserve‑state constraints, and protected interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum membership.

Shared_initial generation and model configuration. To isolate deterministic validator/repair rescue from generator resampling effects we implemented a shared_initial protocol: a single LLM candidate was generated per pair and reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini (requested_model recorded in the archived model configuration). Shared_initial reuse prevents differences due to independent resampling and measures only deterministic validation and bounded repair applied to the identical output.

Validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic netops validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and forbidden‑template protections for protected interfaces. Scoring was binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt; the repair operator was a constrained, localized edit routine limited to sequencing and insertion edits and applied only when the validator flagged the shared_initial candidate. Repaired candidates were deterministically re‑validated; any remaining flag caused a guarded failure for the pair.

Contamination controls and missingness rules. The preregistration included deterministic contamination detection (negative controls and invariant checks). A pair would be excluded from confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls for that pair failed due to provider/infrastructure outage; no such dual‑call exclusions occurred in the confirmatory run. All provider failures, scoring outcomes, and repair traces were logged and archived.

Analysis executor and inferential plan. The preregistered confirmatory analysis used a paired binary executor to compute contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), the absolute paired difference, an exact two‑sided McNemar test, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval. Bootstrap parameters used in the archived analysis were seed = 1729 and resamples B = 10000. Secondary and stratum tests were labeled exploratory and multiplicity‑handled where reported.
sections.results:
Execution integrity and accounting. The registered adapter completed the confirmatory run with 600 completed episodes yielding 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. The run used 301 model‑call events (300 shared_initial generations and a single repair invocation). No provider outages or pair exclusions occurred; deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting.

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300, i.e., baseline = 299/300 (0.9966667) and guarded = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test (operating on discordant counts n10 and n01) returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1), the exact test has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per stratum: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant pair occurred in the high stratum. The validator attributed the initial failure to a sequencing omission (a missing required 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained repair performed a single localized insertion of the missing sequencing command and the validator reported the repaired candidate as valid. Thus the solitary deterministic rescue required one permitted repair invocation.

Contamination, missingness, and cost. Contamination checks flagged no anomalies; no episodes were unscorable and no pairs were excluded. The guarded pipeline produced its single rescue with minimal extra model‑call cost (one additional repair stage across 300 pairs). These counts and diagnostic traces are archived with the run bundle for forensic inspection.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational meaning. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent corresponds to operational policies that constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under such policies the guarded pipeline quantifies deterministic validator/repair rescue applied to the identical candidate. Pipelines that permit resampling, verifier‑guided regeneration, or iterative steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; those workflows must be evaluated under a different preregistered design.

Ceiling effects and the preregistered pilot. The preregistration aimed to detect a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 conditional on estimated discordance from a pilot. The optional pilot was not executed prior to the main run; consequently the baseline single‑shot performance on this synthetic suite was near ceiling (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and limited sensitivity to small absolute improvements. This practical outcome underscores the value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on the chosen task suite.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale in this synthetic suite. The guarded pipeline's marginal utility therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness. Richer validators that check reachability or ACL semantics would likely yield different rescue rates; conversely, if operator policy forbids automated edits, deterministic rescue is limited to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded, low‑cost deterministic rescue. Iterative repairs, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided generation would increase rescue opportunities but address a different estimand and operational cost profile. The archived single repair trace can inform design choices for permitted edit operators and budgets in production CI/CD workflows.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations must align evaluation estimands with operational constraints. If model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful upper bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. If multiple calls are acceptable, evaluations should allow resampling or interactive repair to measure achievable success under that policy.
sections.conclusion: We ran a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Baseline single‑shot generation achieved 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks/topologies were generated by a deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase validator marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
